photos.c: Enfield, 3rd May 1997 and Matt Douglas finds himself sandwiched between Lloyd Cowan (Shaftesbury Barnet) on the far side and Kirk Harries (Puma TVH).  Matt came home 3rd in 14.68.

Left: Matt Douglas, pictured at Copthall during the final BAL match, had a fine season. He neared his best ever of 50.72 in the opening league match, with a 50.9 and by the end of the summer was down to 50.20 in the Commonwealth Games, representing Northern Ireland.

Below: Du'aine Ladejo, Matt Douglas, Geoff Dearman and Sean Baldock (still breathing hard after his last leg stint) enjoy the attention after providing the most dominating display of the evening. It was Du'aine's last race before signing for Birchfield Harriers.

Front Page: Matt Douglas always gives everything in his races - whether League, Championship or Olympic Games. The year 2000 saw him take his best 400 metre hurdles time below 50 for the first time and he ended the season second only, in Britain, to our own Chris Rawlinson, and well into the World's Top 50.
Welcome back to Matt!  Having won the previous evening in Bangor, Northern Ireland, Matt Douglas flew in to Manchester to do the business for the British League team.  Photo by Pat Mead.
Above: Overlooked for international duty, Matt Douglas stormed the ten barriers as if they personally had slighted him.
Above: Matt Douglas hands the baton to Will Sharman for the last leg of the last race - the 4 x 400m relay.
